equity_bridge.item: Vega Therapeutics upfront consideration (closed July 2026, after 2026-03-31 balance sheet)
equity_bridge.note: Analysis JSON recent_developments 2026-07; ~$1.25B cash upfront. Up to $750M sales-based milestones excluded as contingent.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR implied by the driver path (FY2025 5,141 -> FY2035 ~5,230); trailing CAGRs are deliberately NOT used because the Dec-2028 Jakafi LOE makes the past a poor predictor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (5.7%) diverges >30% from revenue 3yr (14.8%) and EPS 3yr (62.7%): the FY2024 $2.0B Dutch tender removed ~$2B of book equity, and EPS is off a depressed FY2022 base ($1.53). Neither is a growth signal.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC incl. equity-award taxes - interest income, $M): FY2020 -512.7 (MorphoSys $805M upfront expensed; interest income not in dataset pre-2022, treated as 0), FY2021 355.6, FY2022 636.9, FY2023 61.1 (Section 174 cash-tax spike), FY2024 -186.0 (Escient ~$750M acquired IPR&D expensed through OCF), FY2025 922.8. Reported FCF over the same years: -312.0, 568.5, 892.1, 464.0, 249.1, 1,354.6. The 5-year owner-FCF CAGR is undefined (negative start) and the 3-year figure (13.2% from FY2022) is below the reported-FCF 3-year CAGR (15.0%): SBC+withholding grew from 214.7 to 326.2 (+52%) while reported FCF grew +52% too, so the gap is mostly interest income on the growing cash pile. Capex FY2023-25 backfilled into core_metrics via make fix from us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireOtherProductiveAssets (32.5, 86.3, 58.9).

scenario_narratives.base: Incyte is a one-drug company with a dated cliff: Jakafi is ~62% of revenue and ruxolitinib composition-of-matter exclusivity (with pediatric extension) ends around December 2028. The base case takes management's FY2026 guidance at the midpoint, lets Opzelura and the hematology/oncology growth products (Niktimvo, Monjuvi/Minjuvi, Zynyz, Pemazyre) compound at ~20% into the cliff, then applies standard oral small-molecule generic erosion to Jakafi (-60% in year one, -45% in year two) and to the Novartis Jakavi royalty. Non-Jakafi product revenue reaches ~$3.2B in 2030, the low end of management's $3-4B target, so total revenue troughs at ~$4.3B in FY2030 -- below FY2024 -- with the adjusted EBITDA margin compressing to 22% because R&D is held near $2B to fund the replacement pipeline. Owner FCF falls from ~$1.2B pre-cliff to ~$0.4B in the trough and rebuilds to ~$1.0B by FY2035. The valuation is dominated by the recovered post-LOE business capitalised at 15x, not by the pre-cliff cash flows, and the $3.4B net cash (less $1.25B for Vega) is ~$10/share of the answer.
scenario_narratives.bull: The bull axes are franchise retention and pipeline conversion. Jakafi XR (once-daily, approved 2026) converts enough of the MF/PV/GVHD base that IR generic entry erodes the franchise 45% rather than 60%, and the ex-US royalty tails hold longer. Opzelura's EU launch in moderate atopic dermatitis (positive CHMP, late 2026) plus HS and prurigo nodularis label expansions sustain +25% growth; Niktimvo becomes the standard in chronic GVHD; and at least two of povorcitinib, INCB123667 (ovarian) and latarcibart (VWD, from Vega) launch by FY2030-31. Non-Jakafi revenue hits the top of the $3-4B 2030 target and total revenue regains its FY2028 peak by FY2032, with margins recovering to 37% on a more diversified base. This requires four largely independent things to go right, which is why its weight is below the house default.
scenario_narratives.bear: The bear axes are pre-cliff share loss and post-cliff replacement failure. GSK's Ojjaara (momelotinib) keeps taking anaemic-MF share so Jakafi flattens before the cliff; the ~$246M Medicaid settlement drops out of FY2027 and Opzelura's underlying growth proves to be +10% not +20% as payers restrict a $1B topical; generic ruxolitinib takes 75% of Jakafi in FY2029 and half of what remains in FY2030; and the mid-stage pipeline delivers no launch inside the horizon while R&D is kept at ~$2B to keep trying. Revenue falls to ~$3.3B by FY2030 and the adjusted EBITDA margin drops to 8-12%, meaning near-zero owner FCF after SBC for three years. The company survives comfortably on $2B+ of net cash, but the value is little more than that cash plus a 12x multiple on a ~$0.4B FCF business by FY2035.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Incyte as what it will be after the cliff, not what it earns before it. The explicit 10-year path carries the FY2028 peak, the FY2029-30 trough and the recovery, so no pre-LOE cash flow is capitalised in perpetuity. SBC and equity-award withholding (~6.3% of revenue) are expensed and rise as a share of revenue through the trough because compensation does not fall with Jakafi; interest income on the $3.4B cash pile is stripped so the cash is counted once, in the bridge; the Vega upfront is deducted from that cash because it was paid after the balance-sheet date. WACC is held at 8.5% in every scenario and the cliff risk is charged through the scenario paths and a 25/50/25 weighting -- once, not twice.
key_risks_to_valuation: Jakafi generic erosion speed and depth after Dec-2028 (base assumes -60% then -45%; every 10pp of first-year retention is worth roughly $3-4/share)
Whether non-Jakafi product revenue reaches $3-4B by 2030 -- the base takes the low end; a miss is the bear case
The FY2029-31 adjusted EBITDA margin trough (22% base) depends on how fast opex is cut against a held-flat ~$2B R&D budget
Terminal cap of 15x FY2035 owner FCF: the largest single input; the value is ~55-60% terminal
Further large business development (Incyte spent $750M in 2024 and $1.25B in 2026 on acquired IPR&D) is not modelled beyond Vega and would reduce net cash further
The Q2 2026 balance sheet is not yet in the dataset; net cash is a March-2026 figure pro-forma for Vega
Flat share count is a convention the company is not currently funding with buybacks (basic count drifting +1.5-2%/yr)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 82.52-132.60
data_sources.financials: INCY_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, millions USD, FY2008-Q1 2026) plus SEC companyfacts for the Q1 2026 10-Q balance sheet, diluted share count, capex tag (PaymentsToAcquireOtherProductiveAssets), equity-award tax withholding and interest income
data_sources.qualitative: INCY_Analysis.json (2026-09-29): FY2026 guidance as raised at Q2 2026, Jakafi LOE ~Dec 2028, Vega Therapeutics acquisition, $3-4B non-Jakafi 2030 target, bull/bear points

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation 249.346 plus us-gaap:PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 76.818 (financing). Incyte publishes no combined equity-award figure in its non-GAAP reconciliation, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average count from the Q1 2026 10-Q (us-gaap:WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding, 206.83M; basic 199.34M; cover page 199.78M at 2026-04-21). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count. Buyback cash was 0 in FY2025 and 9M-2025 (the $2.0B FY2024 Dutch tender was a one-off), so the flat count is a modelling convention not currently being funded -- the basic count has drifted +1.5-2%/yr since the tender.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST, Sep-2026), ERP 5.0%, beta 0.85 (biopharma, LOE-exposed earnings) -> cost of equity ~8.5%. Debt is ~$35M of finance leases against $3.5B cash, so WACC = cost of equity = 8.5%. Held identical across all three scenarios; the Jakafi LOE risk is charged once, through the scenario revenue and margin paths and their weights, not through a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost ($20M liability) is inside operating expenses and therefore inside the EBITDA margin; finance lease liability ($34.7M at FY2025 10-K) is carried in total_debt. No lease_cost_pct_path -- one treatment, not two.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. Incyte has no non-controlling interests.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1: US operating company). Incyte is a specialty biopharma whose value is a stream of product cash flows; not a bank, REIT, LIC or shell, so the default engine applies. No adaptations file needed (USD filer, USD quote, no NCI, immaterial leases, SBC-positive market). ANCHORS: FY0 = FY2025 (revenue 5,141.2; reported FCF 1,354.6 = OCF 1,413.5 - capex 58.9; owner FCF 922.8 after SBC+equity-award taxes 326.2 and interest income 105.6 -- interest stripped because net cash of $3.4B is ~3.7x the FCF base). Balance sheet is the Q1 2026 10-Q (2026-03-31, filed 2026-04-28), the latest in the SEC companyfacts feed; the Q2 2026 10-Q is not yet in the dataset. Cash & equivalents 3,461.1 (no marketable securities held). The ~$1.25B Vega Therapeutics upfront (closed July 2026, after this balance sheet) is deducted in equity_bridge; the up-to-$750M sales milestones are contingent and NOT deducted. Equity stakes in collaborators (Syndax, Agenus, etc.) are excluded from the bridge for conservatism. HORIZON: 10 years (FY2026-FY2035) so that the Dec-2028 Jakafi loss of exclusivity, the FY2029-30 trough and the recovery all sit inside the explicit period; the terminal value capitalises the recovered, post-LOE margin, not the pre-cliff one. FY2026 REVENUE contains a ~$246M one-time NON-CASH Medicaid rebate settlement benefit (reversal of an accrued liability); year-1 margin is set 1pp below the underlying run-rate and wc_capture is negative so the flows do not credit it as cash. FY2026 GAAP opex guidance ($4,915-4,995M) includes the Vega acquired-IPR&D charge; the underlying opex step-up is ~17%, which is what the year-1 margin compression reflects. YEAR-1 SANITY: component build gives owner FCF of ~$1.1B on FY2026 vs $923M actual FY2025; the gap is the FY2025 working-capital/deferred-tax drag (~$230M, OCF 1,413 vs NI+SBC+D&A 1,629), which was partly the Section 174 deferred-tax unwind and is not carried forward at full size. CASH TAX: FY2025 cash taxes were 212 (~13% of pre-tax) after the OBBBA restored domestic R&D expensing; FY2023-24 were abnormally high (Section 174 capitalisation). Ramp 15% -> 20% (21% federal + state, net of R&D credit and FDII). The Vega IPR&D is a 15-year Section 197 amortisation for tax (~$17M/yr shelter) and is ignored. CAPEX 2.0% of revenue = PP&E ~1.2% (FY2023-25 average 1.4%) plus ~0.8% for small recurring in-licensing; larger BD is not modelled beyond Vega, which is a judgment the reader should weigh (Incyte has done a $750M+ deal in 2 of the last 3 years).

bear.growth_rationale: GSK's Ojjaara keeps taking myelofibrosis share pre-cliff (Jakafi flat then down), the one-off drops out of FY2027, Opzelura growth slows to +10% on payer pushback, and generic ruxolitinib erodes Jakafi 75% in FY2029 and 50% again in FY2030. Pipeline (povorcitinib, INCB123667, latarcibart) fails to reach market in the horizon; non-Jakafi product revenue ~$2.5B by 2030, missing the target. Opex cuts lag the revenue fall, so the FY2029-30 margin nears breakeven after SBC.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +12%: product guidance midpoint $5,195M (Jakafi 3,245 + Opzelura 1,075 incl. $246M one-off + Hem/Onc 875) plus ~$560M royalties/other = ~$5.76B. FY2027 +4%: underlying ~+9% (Opzelura and Hem/Onc growth products +20%, Jakafi +3%) less the ~4pp one-off dropping out. FY2028 +6.5%: Jakafi peaks ~$3.4B, non-Jakafi ~$2.95B. FY2029 -28%: US generic ruxolitinib entry after the Dec-2028 LOE erodes Jakafi ~60% in year one (standard oral small-molecule erosion) and Jakavi royalties start to erode on EU expiry, against non-Jakafi +14%. FY2030 -7.5%: Jakafi -45% again to ~$0.75B; non-Jakafi product revenue ~$3.2B, the LOW end of management's $3-4B 2030 target. FY2031-35: +3.5% to +5% then tapering as the diversified portfolio compounds off a $4.3B base.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted (pre-SBC) EBITDA margin was 36.1% in FY2025. FY2026 33%: opex step-up ~17% ex-Vega for launches, 1pp below run-rate to avoid crediting the non-cash Medicaid benefit. FY2028 35%: pre-cliff peak with Jakafi at scale. FY2029-30 22%: revenue -28% while R&D+SG&A can only be cut ~12% then ~7% (R&D held near $2B for the pipeline). Recovery to 31% by FY2035 as non-Jakafi products reach scale -- below the pre-cliff level because the franchise being replaced was a single high-margin drug.

bull.growth_rationale: Jakafi XR conversion retains a meaningful slice of the franchise through the IR generic entry (Jakafi -45% in FY2029, not -60%); Opzelura EU launch (late 2026) and HS/PN label expansions drive +25% growth; Niktimvo/Monjuvi/Zynyz reach the top of the $3-4B 2030 target; povorcitinib and INCB123667 add first launch revenue by FY2030-31. FY2035 revenue ~$7.2B.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the Jakafi loss of exclusivity is a certain event of uncertain magnitude sitting inside the explicit horizon, non-Jakafi products have never been proven at the scale needed to replace it, and Incyte's own history includes pipeline setbacks (Jakafi XR CRL, FY2024 Escient write-off). Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs XR retention, Opzelura EU uptake, Hem/Onc scaling AND at least two pipeline launches to all go right. Base 50% is management's own diversification plan delivered at the low end of its target.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
